title: Bennington Triangle: Where 5 People Vanished in 5 Years
description:
The Bennington Triangle: between 1945 and 1950, five people disappeared in the woods around Glastenbury Mountain in southwestern Vermont, including Bennington College student Paula Jean Welden. This is the full story of the Vermont disappearances, told case by case.

We follow hunter Middie Rivers in 1945, Paula Welden on the Long Trail in 1946, World War One veteran James Tedford in 1949, eight-year-old Paul Jepson and hiker Frieda Langer in 1950, the searches and the few clues left behind, and the theories, from the cold and the terrain to the "Lost Horizon" and the Bennington Monster.

What do you think happened in the Bennington Triangle? Tell me in the comments.

short.caption:
Five people vanished in one corner of Vermont between 1945 and 1950.
Four were never found.
What do you think happened in the Bennington Triangle?
short.narration: You could drive the Vermont roads where 5 people vanished by 1950, but nobody knows what happened to 4 of them. In November 1945, a 74-year-old hunter, Middie Rivers, walked away from camp. He knew these woods, and never came back. Next spring, a hiker found only his handkerchief. A year later, Paula Jean Welden, 18, set out for the Long Trail. She wore a red jacket, jeans and lightweight sneakers. She had nothing warm enough for December. Witnesses saw her near the trail, then nothing. Three years to the day later, a 68-year-old veteran boarded a bus to Bennington. He never arrived. In October 1950, eight-year-old Paul Jepson vanished from his mother's vehicle. A bloodhound tracked him to an intersection, where the scent stopped. Sixteen days later, Frieda Langer took a shortcut back to her cabin. Up to three hundred people searched for her. Her body was found the next spring, the only one ever recovered. People call this place the Bennington Triangle. Some blame the cold and the wild terrain. Others tell stories of something living in the trees. In 1945, a search leader said everyone lost here in recent decades had been found. So what changed after 1945? Tell me what you think happened. The full case file is on StoryVaultFiles.
